newsitem.title: USA: Cal Water shareholders approve stock split.
newsitem.headline: Cal Water shareholders approve stock split.

text.p: California Water Service Co said Wednesday that shareholders at the company's annual meeting approved a two-for-one stock split.

Shareholders also approved the formation of a holding-company structure, in which California Water Service Group will be the parent company. Both actions are expected to become effective after regulatory approval during the second half of 1997.

"A holding-company structure will help us meet the challenges facing investor-owned water utilities in the 21st century," said Chairman Robert Foy. "It will allow the company to be more competitive in providing non-regulated utility services, particularly by facilitating our ability to access capital quickly."

California posted profits for the first quarter, ending March 31, of $2.9 million, or $0.46 a share, compared with $1.2 million, or $0.18 a share in the comparable year-ago period. Revenues rose to $37.5 million from $32.2 million in the year-ago period.
